While it doesn't have quite the same ring as NaNoWriMo, NaProWriMo is the month where instead of writing 50,000 words a day for 30 days for one project. We write 1,667 words a day for thirty different projects.

Sounds doable, right? It is.

Beginning November 1, the first prompt of the month will be posted. In the event that the next prompt fails to appear in 24 hours; consider it extra time for you to continue writing. This will hold true for the remainder of the month.

But most all; Good Luck and Have Fun.

The Prompts

Week I - Rewrites and New Formulations

  • Day 01: Rewrite a classic fairy tale.
  • Day 02: Write a fan-fiction.
  • Day 03: Write about a stranger you see.
  • Day 04: Write in a genre you're unfamiliar with.
  • Day 05: Fictionalized a memory.
  • Day 06: Write the modern fairy tale.
  • Day 07: Write about a successful failure.

Week II - Situations and Settings

  • Day 08: Character gets a virus on his/her computer.
  • Day 09: Your character almost gets hit by a vehicle..
  • Day 10: Your character gets too much money from the ATM machine..
  • Day 11: Waiting for the bus..
  • Day 12: Mugged!
  • Day 13: Your character hasn't slept for three days..
  • Day 14: Undressing the other with thine own eyes..

Week III - Passages and Trains of Thought

  • Day 15: "I have to try.."
  • Day 16: "Remember that time when.."
  • Day 17: "It's not what this looks like.."
  • Day 18: "She had curves in all the wrong places.."
  • Day 19: "Please don't go.."
  • Day 20: "You're horrible, you know that?"
  • Day 21: "He glanced at his watch impatiently.."

Week IV - Locations and Places

  • Day 22: A story that takes place pre-1950.
  • Day 23: A story set in a ghost town.
  • Day 24: A story that takes place 100 years in the future.
  • Day 25: A story taking place during any sporting event.
  • Day 26: A story about space.
  • Day 27: Stories under the ocean.
  • Day 28: Trapped on the thirteen floor.

Week V - The End

  • Day 29: Rewrite that story you've been wanting to redo.
  • Day 30: Expand upon a story you've always liked.

Reddit takes on Kickstarter with crowdfunding site Redditmade

They rolled this out so poorly it was laughable; with the first roll out they were basically using their unpaid mods to vet these campaigns and then giving a cut to reddit inc.

However, they've now implemented a change to the "workflow" (after a mod revolt) such that only moderators can submit subreddit related camapigns and all profits must go to a charity.

What this still allows for, and what may cause major issues, is that a reddit mod could make a campaign not related to the subreddit in question; sticky that campaign and then, in essence, profit off moderating.

This could be a shitstorm in waiting for reddit inc and I'm interested to see how it goes down.
I don't think it will work for reddit. That's just my opinion though. I could easily be wrong.
Did they really restrict it to just the moderators? that's pretty funny as it essentially kills the main reason to use it.(i.e. easy, "risk-free" community campaigns)

Where did all the trick or treaters go?

We've had zero visits but we live in apartment complex which requires a key to get in :p Back in Sweden we've had a few visits last year and I guess I was rather generous as they kept coming back for more (the word on the street spreads :p).

We live across the street from a little "mom and pop" convenience store. The former owner was known far and wide for his generosity on Halloween, goody bags for the kids, cans of soda for the parents. The first Halloween we ran out of candy after about 200 kids, because we didn't know what to expect. The next year, we had enough on hand for about 350, and handed almost all of it out. Then the store changed hands, and the new owners were not that into it. Last year, they handed out pretty much the standard low cost stuff. Word got out, and this year only about 150 kids showed up. It was still better than a lot of folks get, but it bummed me out not seeing all the cute costumes we saw the years before.
